title: Variables & types
description: let, const, and var differ in scope and reassignment — const locks the binding, not the contents.

notes: const locks the binding, not the value — you can still mutate the object or array it points to.
typeof null returns "object" — a famous historical quirk. Test for null with x === null.
var is function-scoped and hoisted; let and const are block-scoped and live in a temporal dead zone until declared.

questions.q: Which of these is legal after `const obj = { n: 1 };`?
questions.explain: const locks the BINDING, not the contents — mutating properties is fine.
A historical bug preserved for compatibility.
var ignores block boundaries — the reference's f() returns 1 even though v was declared inside the if. let or const there would throw ReferenceError.
typeof always evaluates to a STRING, so the answer is the quoted "undefined", not the value undefined. null is the only tag that lies — it reports "object".

hints: typeof is an operator, not a function — no parentheses needed.
